title: Failures: lose an engine, a trainer pod, a whole trainer node
design_ref: Failures and recovery on multi-week runs
purpose: Start a run with checkpoints and a restart policy, break it three ways, and measure how long each takes to recover, how much work is repeated, and what share of the reserved GPU time went into progress.

steps.display: kubectl -n rl-scale get lws rollout   # 2 engine(s), settings: defaults
kubectl apply -f trainer-fail-engine.yaml   # JobSet with failurePolicy.maxRestarts=3; checkpoints every 10 steps; a rollout engine's pod is deleted once the run is past step 14
kubectl delete pod rollout-0-1   # the worker pod of the rollout group
python recovery.py fail-engine   # from the run's records and the pod's log

checks.description: after a rollout engine's pod is deleted, the run goes on and completes all 45 steps without anyone's help
checks.because: The JobSet's failure policy recreates the trainer pod; the new pod restores the newest complete checkpoint from the state bucket and continues. Nobody ran a command.

checks.description: after a rollout engine's pod is deleted, the first step is the one after a checkpoint, and no more than ten steps are repeated
checks.because: A checkpoint is written every ten steps. Work done since the last one is lost; the checkpoint interval is the bound on it.

checks.description: after a rollout engine's pod is deleted, the run is stepping again within fifteen minutes
checks.because: That includes the pod's start, the packages, loading the model and the checkpoint, rebuilding the NCCL group with the fleet, and a first step.

checks.description: after the trainer's pod is deleted, the run goes on and completes all 45 steps without anyone's help
checks.because: The JobSet's failure policy recreates the trainer pod; the new pod restores the newest complete checkpoint from the state bucket and continues. Nobody ran a command.

checks.description: after the trainer's pod is deleted, the first step is the one after a checkpoint, and no more than ten steps are repeated

checks.description: the checkpoint came from the bucket, not from the node that failed (node drill)
checks.because: The node's own disk went with the node. What survives is the copy the trainer's background thread made.

checks.description: losing an engine is not absorbed: the trainer's process ends and is restarted too (finding)
checks.because: The design assumes a failed rollout engine is replaced while the run continues. With NCCL weight transfer the engines and the trainer share one communicator, and a lost member stops every collective. The JobSet restarted the trainer; I did not capture whether its own error or its watchdog ended it, because the replaced pod's log is gone.
